_comment: Ten of the adult panel's headline metrics -- appeal, child appeal, ask-to-see,
recommend, theatrical intent, streaming intent, category interest -- arrive as
prose with no closed-end anywhere. They cannot enter a banner as they stand.
Each rubric maps prose to a 5-point favourability scale. Cues are regexes; the
highest-|weight| match wins, and a negation inside the 4 words before a cue
flips it. Every score carries the cue that produced it, so a wrong number is
This is a BASELINE, deliberately: it is what makes the AI pass checkable. Run
it first, read the distribution, then run out/load/08_ai_prose_score.sql and
compare. If they disagree by more than a few points of top box, one of them is
wrong and you can see which sentence caused it.

not_applicable is separate from unscored on purpose. 169 NPRECO answers read 'N/A - I am a parent': the harness forced every persona through both the parent and non-parent recommend paths, and the personas themselves flagged the ones that did not apply. Those rows are evidence that the base is wrong, not answers that the rubric failed to read.
